title: Reference Brief
summary: Keep only the evidence that materially changes the answer or required format.
learnerGoal: Build a compact package for a vendor recommendation brief.
taskAudience: Procurement lead choosing a short-listed vendor
whyMatters: Reference-heavy work often fails because useful-looking background crowds out the few excerpts that actually drive the recommendation.
taskBrief: Prepare an AI-ready package to draft a vendor recommendation brief. The brief must compare security fit, price band, and service commitments for a final shortlist memo.
successCriteria: Includes evidence that directly affects the recommendation.
Summarizes long but relevant background instead of pasting it whole.
Keeps conditional legal detail retrievable rather than bloating the package.
Omits history and marketing copy that do not change the recommendation.
quickPredictionPrompt: What makes a reference excerpt worth paying for in your token budget?
dynamicFacts: Procurement needs a shortlist memo, not a full technical evaluation
Security fit is slightly more important than price
outputContract: Return sections: Recommendation / Why It Fits / What Needs Follow-up
Base the memo on provided evidence only
Call out any remaining conditional questions

cards.title: Security Certification Summary
cards.excerpt: Vendor A completed the required identity and data-handling certification checks. Vendor B still has one open control exception.
cards.summaryText: Directly affects security fit for the shortlist.

cards.title: Pricing Comparison Table
cards.excerpt: Vendor A is mid-band pricing. Vendor B is lower priced but adds support fees beyond pilot volume.

cards.title: Customer Support SLA Excerpt
cards.excerpt: Vendor A commits to named response times and escalation paths for pilot incidents.

cards.title: Feature Brochure
cards.excerpt: Long marketing language covering every product capability, many of which are out of scope for the shortlist memo.
cards.summaryText: Broad marketing copy is not decision-driving.

cards.title: Analyst Review Digest
cards.excerpt: Analyst notes are directionally helpful but do not outweigh direct certification, pricing, and SLA evidence.
cards.summaryText: Helpful context, but not core evidence.

cards.title: Legal Terms Appendix
cards.excerpt: Detailed contractual fallback terms that matter only if the team proceeds to contract drafting.
cards.summaryText: Valuable later, not needed in the core recommendation package.

cards.title: Company History Sheet
cards.excerpt: Founding story, office count, and partnership timeline.

cards.title: Implementation Note
cards.excerpt: Pilot setup for Vendor A is simpler because SSO mapping is pre-validated for the existing environment.
cards.summaryText: Useful implementation context, but summary is enough.

cards.title: Old Pricing Email
cards.excerpt: Quotes an earlier price that predates current support-fee structure.

commentary: Keep the brief anchored on security fit, pricing, and SLA commitments.
Summarize useful context that helps explain the recommendation but does not need verbatim inclusion.
Defer legal detail to follow-up instead of spending core budget on it now.
Exclude stale and background-heavy material that does not change the shortlist decision.

bonusBranches.title: Stricter Budget Replay
bonusBranches.description: Re-run the vendor brief with a tighter budget and force harder selection discipline.
bonusBranches.coachNote: Protect the certification, pricing, and SLA evidence first. Supporting material should shrink or move out.

overlayCards.title: Procurement Memo Template
overlayCards.excerpt: Shortlist memo should focus on security fit, price band, and pilot support readiness. Leave marketing breadth out.
overlayCards.summaryText: Compact memo framing for the strict-budget replay.

commentary: The stricter-budget replay should protect only the few cards that directly change the answer.
Compact replay-only constraint cards can shape the answer without demanding another full direct include.
Older background and follow-up material should move into Summarize, Retrieve Later, or Omit much earlier than in the core run.

bonusBranches.title: Authority vs Freshness Drill
bonusBranches.description: Re-run the brief while resisting polished but weaker secondary commentary when current source materials are already available.
bonusBranches.coachNote: Keep source documents in front. Secondary analyst or implementation commentary can support the brief, but it should not lead it.

overlayCards.title: Security Review Ticket — Today
overlayCards.excerpt: Vendor B still has one open control exception. The shortlist memo should not present its security posture as fully cleared.
overlayCards.summaryText: Fresh security evidence for the authority-versus-freshness replay.

commentary: The authority-versus-freshness replay should make current source-of-record evidence visibly lead the answer.
Branch-only fresh evidence should change what the best package looks like, not just how the coaching sounds.
Comfortable but aging summaries can support the answer, but they should not steer it.

compoundChecks.teachingNote: A good shortlist memo keeps recommendation logic, caveats, and remaining follow-up obligations together instead of smoothing any one of them away.

reviewCoaching.message: Do not let the cheaper-looking vendor erase the security and support-fee caveats that still shape the recommendation.
A shortlist memo is incomplete if it sounds final while real follow-up is still required.
Security-first logic, Vendor B caveats, and explicit follow-up should stay together instead of being smoothed apart.
